solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some measurement taken from copper-covered seat

indicators.note: a copper-covered seat is one with the copper wrapped round it, so the seat goes inside

parts.note: PC, police constable, is a copper
the arse is what you sit on, a seat

explanation.surface: Someone takes a reading from a chair upholstered in copper.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsec is a unit of astronomical distance, about 3.26 light years, so it is one kind of measurement.

clue.text: An artist embodies attendant spirit in Turkish city

indicators.note: to embody is to contain within one body, so the spirit goes inside

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
in Egyptian belief the ka is a person's spiritual double accompanying them

explanation.surface: A painter carries a guardian spirit around a Turkish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara is the capital of Turkey, one of its major cities.

clue.text: Occasionally saying academic work becomes pastiche?

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of saying is used

parts.note: a thesis is a piece of academic work for a degree

explanation.surface: A remark that a scholar's work is now and then mere imitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche combines borrowed elements into one work, so loosely it is a blend or combination, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Miserable chap tucking into toast

indicators.note: the chap is tucked into the toast, placed inside it

parts.note: cheers is the word said in a toast
Les is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A gloomy man digs into his toast at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toast' looks like bread but is the drinking toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerless means gloomy and joyless, a synonym for wretched or unhappy.

clue.text: Worst and best locations to pause excursion?

parts.note: the pits is slang for the very worst
the tops is slang for the very best

explanation.surface: A guide ranks the worst and best spots to stop during a day trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The excursion is a motor race: pit stops are where cars pull in mid-race, and the question mark flags that loose reading.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing, pit stops are the places a car halts during its run for fuel and tyres.

clue.text: Security measure in flat on Strand

parts.note: a pad is a flat or apartment, in slang
a lock is a strand of hair

explanation.surface: A safety precaution in an apartment on the Strand, the London street.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a famous London street, but here 'Strand' means a strand of hair, and 'on' puts the flat above it in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A padlock is a detachable lock used to keep a door, gate or locker secure.

clue.text: Rwandan king of old is on the rise

parts.note: Tut, Tutankhamun, is an ancient Egyptian king

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: An old Rwandan monarch is becoming more prominent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are one of the main ethnic groups of Rwanda, so a Tutsi is a Rwandan.

clue.text: Go round one base for carmakers

indicators.note: go round means the word for go is put round one

parts.note: a turn is a go, as in a game
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Drive round a single base used by car manufacturers.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin in Italy is the home of Fiat, so it is the headquarters city of a big car firm.

clue.text: Topless time at Indian city causes itching

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its top, its first letter in a down answer

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: Sunbathing topless in an Indian city brings on an itchy rash.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: itchy, scaly skin is a symptom of this disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Pellagra is a niacin-deficiency disease whose dermatitis brings rough, irritated, itchy skin.

clue.text: Aggressive sort had Nikes made specially

indicators.note: something made specially is built to order, so these letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: A thug wore trainers that were custom-made for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinheads, the shaven-headed youth subculture, are stereotyped as violent troublemakers.

clue.text: Time to race along — hard going for swimmer

indicators.note: with hard going, the letter for hard leaves the word for racing along

parts.note: to hurtle is to race along at speed
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A racer is told it's time to speed along, though the going is tough.
explanation.definitionFit: A turtle is a marine reptile that spends its life swimming in the sea.

clue.text: Unearth urn that contains legendary figure

indicators.note: the run of words Unearth urn contains the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: An archaeologist is told to dig up a burial urn holding a famous person's remains.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur of Camelot is the hero of British legend, so he is a legendary figure.

clue.text: Gold cases for instance not all from China?

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: the cases of words are their outer letters, the shell round the middle, so each word gives its first and last

explanation.surface: Gold boxes, for example, are not all made in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link here; 'cases' takes the ends of instance, not and all. The question mark admits China is only one oriental country.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental means Eastern, from the Orient; China is one example of an Eastern land, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Musical talent demands attention

definitions.meaning: to have an ... for music is to have musical talent
to give someone your ... is to give them attention

explanation.definitionFit: Ear means both the ability to hear pitch well and a listening, as in lend an ear.

clue.text: Ask at retreat to get cooked dish

indicators.note: letters that are cooked are worked over and reshaped, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks to withdraw to a back room to get a meal prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that this dish is famously served raw, so 'cooked' can only be the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak tartare is a dish of raw minced beef, usually served with a raw egg yolk.

clue.text: Not taking booze away — can stored inside

indicators.note: the can is stored inside the word for away

parts.note: absent means away
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A teetotaller clears off, with a can kept hidden on him.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstinent person refrains from alcohol, a teetotaller.

clue.text: Neo thinks about hot bananas thus being tasty

indicators.note: the setter's opinion goes about, around, the rest

parts.note: Neo is the setter, and what Neo thinks is so to me, in my view

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild

parts.note: so means thus

explanation.surface: The setter reckons hot bananas make a delicious dish.
explanation.walkthrough: TO ME is split round OTH (the anagram of HOT) plus SO. Neo confirmed 'Neo thinks' stands for 'to me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome means delicious and appetising, a synonym for tasty.

clue.text: Tree feller an elected council member

parts.note: the alder is a tree
feller is slang for fellow, a man

explanation.surface: A lumberjack who fells trees is a local councillor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree feller' reads as a woodcutter, but 'feller' is slang for a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman is a senior councillor in local government in Britain and the US.

clue.text: Partner having succeeded in checks, leave everything ready

indicators.note: succeeded is placed in the word for partner

parts.note: an ally is a partner
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
to stem is to check or stop a flow
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Once the partner has passed inspection, everyone can leave, all prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: All systems go is the launch-control idiom meaning everything is prepared and set to start.

clue.text: Mythical creature one's not seen at this time

indicators.note: with the one not seen, that letter is missing from the creature

parts.note: the yeti is the mythical abominable snowman
one's reads as one is, and one is I

explanation.surface: The fabled beast has not been spotted so far.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet means up to now, so far, as in not yet arrived.

clue.text: Johnson's rising importance in surrounding area?

definitions.note: read as Johnson is, so the answer describes him rather than naming him

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: note means importance, as in a person of note

indicators.note: in surrounds the letter for area

explanation.surface: Johnson's growing prominence in the local area is questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson went to Eton College, the English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: An Etonian is a pupil or old boy of Eton College, which Boris Johnson attended.

clue.text: What happens at midday makes improvements?

definitions.meaning: at noon a.m. ends, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to correct or better a text, and split as AM ENDS it is noon, when morning finishes.

clue.text: Rightly awaiting execution, but comfortable

parts.note: well means properly, rightly
a task still to do is awaiting execution, i.e. not yet carried out

explanation.surface: A prisoner on death row, justly condemned, is nonetheless at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do describes the prosperous, and comfortable is the idiom for being financially secure.

clue.text: Good to stop real rampaging mammoth

indicators.note: good is used to stop up, plug, the middle of the scrambled word
rampaging means running wild, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A decent person halts a real woolly mammoth on the rampage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mammoth' reads as the animal but is the adjective. 'rampaging' makes LARE from REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth as an adjective means huge, a synonym for big.

clue.text: Anything covering wings of little bird?

indicators.note: the word for anything covers, goes round, the wings

parts.note: owt is northern English dialect for anything

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its outer letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A question about whether anything covers a small bird's wings.
explanation.walkthrough: OWT is Yorkshire dialect for anything. 'little' serves both the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young or small owl, so it is a little bird.

clue.text: Bury is brutal and virtually obliterated

indicators.note: something obliterated is wiped out, so these letters go from the word for brutal

parts.note: inhumane means brutal

indicators.note: virtually means almost all, so the word and loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A town in Lancashire is described as savage and all but destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a Lancashire town, but here it is the verb. 'virtually' leaves AN from 'and', and 'obliterated' takes that AN out of INHUMANE.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhume is a formal word meaning to inter a body in the ground.

clue.text: Lacking ethical sense, sent back large bouquet

indicators.note: sent back means the pieces are read in reverse order, backwards

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a bouquet is the aroma of a wine

explanation.surface: Someone without scruples returned a big bunch of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral describes a person with no moral principles at all, unconcerned by right and wrong.

clue.text: Going towards frozen water, or stuck in it?

parts.note: ice is frozen water
bound for somewhere means going towards it

explanation.surface: A ship is either heading for the ice or already trapped there.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as bound for ice; the definition makes 'it' the same frozen water.
explanation.definitionFit: Icebound describes a ship or harbour held fast by ice and unable to move.

clue.text: Bachelor, inside left, winner always

indicators.note: bachelor is placed inside the word for left

parts.note: food left on the plate is uneaten

explanation.surface: A football commentary: the bachelor playing inside left is a perpetual winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside left' is an old football position, but here 'inside' is the insertion signal and 'left' the leftover food.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that is unbeaten has never lost, so it has won or at least avoided defeat every time.

clue.text: One advocating belief in article first?

parts.note: the is the definite article
1ST is the abbreviation for first, with the numeral read as I

explanation.surface: A writer argues that faith should come first in a newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist holds belief in a god or gods, the opposite of an atheist.
